notes: Copy from Firth's photograph (Pls. VIII, IX). Griffith's translation: 'The honourable Wayekiye, truly beloved(?) of Shipeshiye and Qeresamaye, kin of Maleme the strategus, kin of Maqel-Teqaye the strategus in Bezewe, kin of Pakheme the great qeren, kin of Beke the Agent, kin of the shanapatete-cadet, kin of Matewawe the strategus of the azab ...'; then three more phrases, the invocation to Isis and Osiris (woSi : Soreyi) and formula G. His notes: l. 2, ':to' at the beginning is corrected outside the line to ':ye', and 'the first m [of mdemdeto] looks more like t'; l. 8 'Snptete' may contain the name of Napata; l. 9 Matewawe = Manitawawe of 97/5; l. 10 'penn', cf. 94/13, 29; l. 11 'the first character may be a numeral resembling that in 98/17, 101/8' (printed as the a-sign split in two, each half queried; counted here as one queried a); l. 13 the strokes '×IIII' are a numeral (regnal date or age?), written {×}{4}. In type line 12 the te is printed with a dot under its stroke (te or to?). The word yetmdelo broken across type lines 9-10 is kept whole. be(7)ke is joined across the line number after Griffith's 'Beke'; his translation also reads 'Qeresamaye' and 'qeren' as single words where the type prints qoresm ye and qore N. [Signs read: 243; marked '?': 5 (4 carry Griffith's printed '?', 1 are my doubts)]. '(n)' in text_std is Griffith's superscript stone-line number.

object: rock graffito on a fallen block, over a rude figure of a man on a horse, camel or other animal
site: Dakka: isolated table-shaped hill south of Gebel Abu Dirwa, three miles south-west of the temple (Lower Nubia), south side of the hill
notes: Rock graffito in archaic style, one of three found by O. Bates (Archaeological Survey of Nubia, Bulletin 5); Griffith's hand-copies of November 1910 and Firth's photographs (Pls. XI, XII). The letter in rem is Griffith's sub-number (91 a, b, c); REM's own form of the suffix was not checked. Griffith: 'doubtless a proper name, Yilin, with the common termination qo'; the n-sign is 10 cm high. The type is letter-spaced, so the word division follows Griffith's analysis (name + qo). [Signs read: 6; marked '?': 0 (0 carry Griffith's printed '?', 0 are my doubts)]. '(n)' in text_std is Griffith's superscript stone-line number.
